title: Checking and Changing Lists with in, remove, and pop
content:
What problem does this solve?
Inventories change mid-adventure: check whether you already carry a torch, drop a used potion, or take the first item from a loot pile. Lists come with operations that search and mutate in place.

Basic syntax
  "torch" in inventory
  inventory.remove("potion")
  first = inventory.pop(0)

What actually happens
in asks whether a value is present. remove deletes the first matching value. pop removes by index (default: last item) and gives you the removed value. All three change or inspect the same list object.

When this is useful
Use in before acting on an item, remove when you know the value, pop when the position matters.
concepts: in tests membership without knowing the index
remove deletes the first matching value from the list
pop removes by index and returns the removed item

examples.title: Check before equipping
examples.explanation: in returns True because torch is already in the list.

examples.title: Use a potion
examples.explanation: remove deletes the first potion; the list shrinks in place.

common_mistakes: Calling remove with a value that is not in the list — Python raises ValueError
Expecting remove to return the list — it returns None
Forgetting that pop(0) shifts remaining items to lower indexes

exercises.title: Predict what pop returns
exercises.prompt: What does the first print show — the value removed by pop(0)? Trace the call, then click Check.
exercises.failure_message: pop(0) removes and returns the first element — sword — before the second print runs.
hints: pop(0) removes the item at index 0.
That item is the first name in the list.

exercises.title: Check for a torch
exercises.prompt:
inventory is already created. If "torch" is in inventory, print exactly:
ready

Otherwise print exactly:
missing
hints: Wrap the test in if / else.
Print ready when the torch is present, missing otherwise.

tests.message: Use if / else to branch on membership.

exercises.title: Fix the remove call
exercises.prompt:
After using a potion, the inventory should be ["sword", "key"]. The remove call uses the wrong value and raises ValueError.

Run to see the error, fix the argument to remove, then Check.
hints: Run first — ValueError means the value is not in the list.
Compare each string carefully: potion vs potions.
Remove "potion" exactly as it appears in the list.

tests.name: inventory
tests.message: Use inventory.remove(...) — do not replace the whole list.

tests.name: inventory
tests.message: After removing the potion, inventory should hold sword and key.

exercises.title: Remove an item if present
exercises.prompt:
Write drop_item(inventory, item) that removes item from the list when it is present.

If item is not in inventory, leave the list unchanged. Return the list (same object is fine). Do not print.
exercises.success_message: You checked membership before mutating the list — the safe pattern for inventory changes.
hints: Use in to test before removing.
Only call remove when the item is present — otherwise ValueError.

tests.message: Removing potion should leave sword and key.
Dropping a missing item should not change the list.
An empty inventory should stay empty.
remove deletes only the first matching value.
